# StarPDF v0.10 interactive producer corpus

All files were authored locally from the adjacent deterministic generators on 2026-08-20. They contain only synthetic regression content. Metadata below comes from the parsed catalog/page/field/annotation/font structures, PDF headers, xref markers, EOF count, and producer dictionaries; it is not inferred from filenames.

The Apple fixtures use the installed PDFKit annotation API and Quartz PDFContext serializer. PDFKit emits widget annotations without a catalog `/AcroForm`; they are therefore recorded as bounded orphan-widget recovery cases, not canonical AcroForms. The pdf-lib files are canonical nested AcroForms. Apple PDFKit is an independent authoring API from the earlier Quartz/CUPS print fixtures, while sharing Apple's Quartz serializer.

Every row runs open, page enumeration, text extraction, form and annotation enumeration, supported Square appearance generation, byte-prefix-preserving incremental export, StarPDF reopen, and semantic reinspection in `compatibility_v0_10_tests.rs`. The browser suite performs an exported PDF.js reopen/render for every row and targeted visual deltas for text, checkbox, radio, choice, rotated widget, FreeText, Highlight, Line, and unrelated-appearance preservation.

Across the complete v0.9 + v0.10 corpus there are 21 committed producer fixtures. The existing `test-assets/smartpdf-form.pdf` is the twenty-second meaningful compatibility fixture and continues to supply an additional pdf-lib AcroForm regression. Producer families represented are Chrome/Skia, LibreOfficeDev, Quartz/CUPS, Apple PDFKit annotation authoring, and pdf-lib.

Corpus font scan: CFF 0, CFF2 0, non-Identity Type0 encodings 0. All observed Type0 encodings are Identity-H with ToUnicode. Consequently, v0.10 tests CFF/CFF2/unknown program classification with deterministic synthetic font streams and retains typed mutation refusal; it does not claim corpus-proved CFF writing or a new composite mapping.
